title: International Trade & Supply Chain
completion_message: ¡Soberbio! El comercio internacional mueve el mundo. Vocabulario como 'supply chain', 'procurement' y 'tariffs' te equipa para negociar con proveedores globales y entender la macroeconomía que afecta a tu empresa.

stages.title: Comercio Internacional y Cadena de Suministro (C1)

parts.visual:
La Cadena de Suministro (Supply Chain): 
- Supply chain (Cadena de suministro / El proceso desde la materia prima hasta el cliente). 
Ej: The pandemic severely disrupted the global supply chain. 
- Procurement (Adquisiciones / Compras corporativas de bienes y servicios). 
Ej: The procurement department negotiated a better deal with our suppliers. 
- Logistics (Logística / La organización y movimiento de productos). 
Ej: We outsourced our logistics to a third-party company.
parts.audio: The Supply Chain. The 'Supply chain' is the sequence of processes involved in the production and distribution of a commodity. For example: The pandemic severely disrupted the global supply chain. 'Procurement' is the action of obtaining or purchasing equipment, materials, or services for a business. For example: The procurement department negotiated a better deal with our suppliers. 'Logistics' refers to the detailed organization and implementation of a complex operation, like moving goods. For example: We outsourced our logistics to a third-party company.

parts.visual:
Comercio Global y Aduanas: 
- Tariffs (Aranceles / Impuestos a las importaciones o exportaciones). 
Ej: The new tariffs on steel will increase our manufacturing costs. 
- Customs (Aduanas / La autoridad que controla el flujo de bienes). 
Ej: Our shipment has been stuck in customs for two weeks. 
- Freight (Flete o carga / Bienes transportados por camión, tren, barco o avión). 
Ej: Sea freight is much cheaper than air freight, but slower.
parts.audio: Global Trade and Customs. 'Tariffs' are taxes or duties to be paid on a particular class of imports or exports. For example: The new tariffs on steel will increase our manufacturing costs. 'Customs' refers to the official department that administers and collects the duties levied by a government on imported goods. For example: Our shipment has been stuck in customs for two weeks. 'Freight' refers to goods transported in bulk by truck, train, ship, or aircraft. For example: Sea freight is much cheaper than air freight, but slower.

stages.title: Interactive Quiz
stages.description: Elige el término de logística o comercio internacional correcto.

questions.question: The entire process of making and selling commercial goods is the ____ chain. (Cadena de suministro).
The process of finding, agreeing terms, and buying goods or services from an external source is ____. (Adquisiciones/Compras corporativas).
The government imposed heavy ____ on imported cars to protect local manufacturers. (Aranceles).
questions.explanation: Tariffs = aranceles / impuestos de importación o exportación.

questions.question: The goods are currently being inspected by ____ at the border. (Aduanas).
Goods transported in bulk by truck, train, ship, or aircraft are called ____. (Flete / Carga).
questions.explanation: Freight = flete o mercancía de carga.

questions.question: A person or company that provides goods or services is a ____. (Proveedor).
A person or company that sells goods to the public in relatively small quantities for use or consumption rather than for resale is a ____. (Minorista).
questions.explanation: Retailer = minorista (ej. un supermercado o tienda de ropa).

questions.question: A person or company that sells goods in large quantities at low prices, typically to retailers, is a ____. (Mayorista).
The commercial activity of transporting goods to customers is ____. (Logística).
A large building where raw materials or manufactured goods may be stored before their export or distribution for sale is a ____. (Almacén).
The complete list of items such as property, goods in stock, or the contents of a building is the ____. (Inventario).
A trade ____ is a restriction placed on the trade of goods or services between countries. (Embargo/Barrera).
questions.explanation: Trade barrier = barrera comercial (como un arancel o cuota).

questions.question: An official ban on trade or other commercial activity with a particular country is an ____. (Embargo).
The difference in value between a country's imports and exports is the balance of ____. (Balanza comercial).
A raw material or primary agricultural product that can be bought and sold, such as copper or coffee, is a ____. (Materia prima / Producto básico).
questions.explanation: Commodity = producto básico, materia prima comercializable (ej. oro, petróleo, café).

questions.question: To send goods to another country for sale is to ____ them. (Exportar).
A limited quantity of a particular product that under official controls can be produced, exported, or imported is a ____. (Cuota).
An agent who buys and sells goods for others is a ____. (Corredor / Intermediario).
questions.explanation: Broker (e.g., customs broker) = corredor, agente, intermediario.

questions.question: A document issued by a carrier to acknowledge receipt of cargo for shipment is a Bill of ____. (Conocimiento de embarque).
questions.explanation: Bill of Lading (B/L) = conocimiento de embarque (documento legal de logística).

questions.question: The system of producing and delivering products exactly when they are needed is ____-in-time manufacturing. (Justo a tiempo).
questions.explanation: Just-in-time (JIT) = sistema justo a tiempo (para reducir inventario).

stages.title: Written Expression

questions.question: The ____ chain. (Cadena de suministro con S)
The ____ department. (Adquisiciones/compras con P)
Import ____. (Aranceles con T)
Stuck in ____. (Aduanas con C)
Air ____. (Flete/carga aérea con F)
A reliable ____. (Proveedor con S)
A large ____. (Almacén con W)
Track the ____. (Inventario con I)
Trade ____. (Embargo comercial con E)
Gold is a ____. (Materia prima/producto básico con C)
